claims.text: Conventional processing of single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Spark plasma sintering can fully sinter and consolidate single-phase ZrB2 at 1800–2000 °C.
SPS at 1800–2000 °C will produce lower residual porosity than conventional processing above 2300 °C.
The SPS intervention uses controlled pressure, vacuum or inert atmosphere, rapid heating, and minimal dwell time.
Minimal dwell time at peak temperature will avoid excessive grain growth.
SPS will cause rapid and uniform densification of ZrB2.
Rapid SPS densification will limit grain growth and pore formation.
Pulsed electric current during SPS accelerates mass transport and diffusion in ZrB2.
Accelerated mass transport and diffusion enable effective ZrB2 consolidation at lower temperatures than conventional sintering.
Avoiding prolonged high-temperature exposure minimizes pore formation.
A denser ZrB2 microstructure has fewer initiation sites for damage induced by a liquid plating bath.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have mechanical strength similar to or better than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will develop fewer holes and defects during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
SPS processing will improve the long-term service reliability of single-phase ZrB2 in a liquid plating bath.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 exhibits higher porosity and grain coarsening than the proposed SPS material.
Higher porosity and grain coarsening in conventionally sintered ZrB2 can lead to defects during extended liquid-plating exposure.
